5. The High Court Division has totally ignored the above guidelines and made the above findings and observations which were not at all called for in disposing of such a petition. Though we are reluctant to explore the provisions of law at this stage of the proceeding, since the High Court Division has made those observations after analyzing some provisions of law, we are constrained to clarify the position of law with view to remove doubt. At the outset, we would like to observe that the views taken by the High Court Division are not at all sound and also not conformity with law. The High Court Division ought to have understood the scheme of the law and considered all laws relevant to resolve the point in controversy. Instead, it forms its opinion upon analyzing some sections of Act of 1958 and the Ains of 2004 and 2012. 

 16. There is provision in the Ain of 2004 that subject to its provisions, the provisions of the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958 shall be applicable for the trial of the offences under the AM, 2004. Sub-section (7) of section 5 of Act of 1958 empowers the Special Judge to follow the provisions of the Code for the purpose of framing charge. As per section-6, it is provided that Chapter XX of the Code shall apply to trial of cases in so far as they are not inconsistent with the provisions of the Act of 1958. This Act is also totally silent about the mode of investigation of the offences specified in the schedule and therefore, the provisions of the Code will regulate the procedure. 

 29. The High Court Division unnecessarily considered sections 3, 9 and 12 of Money Laundering Protirodh Ain, 2012, sections 28 and 32 of the Durnity Daman Commission Ain and section 6(3) of the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958 and also the cases of Nasir Uddin Mahmood vs Momtaz Uddin Ahmed, 36 DLR (AD) 14, Khandaker Nasim Uddin Ahmed vs State, 33 DLR (SC) 154, Anti-Corruption Commission vs Dr Mohiuddin Khan Alamgir, 62 DLR (AD) 290, which are not at all relevant for resolving the point in dispute. In view of what stated above, the observations of the High Court Division as quoted above in sub-paragraphs 1-9 are hereby expunged. We hold that an officer of the Durnity Daman Commission or a police officer deputed by the Commission to investigate or inquire into a case in respect of any of the offences mentioned in the schedule to the Ain of 2004, if he has a reasonable ground to believe that any person has been concerned with any of the offences or against whom a reasonable complaint or an FIR has been made or creditable information has been received or a reasonable suspicion exist of his having been so concerned may arrest the offender with the prior approval of the Commission. He may also arrest an offender without prior permission in case of emergency as mentioned above. This petition is disposed of with the above expunction and observations.
